points.quote: Each assessment is marked as ‘Red’, ‘Amber’ or ‘Green’ and this tells you how you can use AI in that assignment.
points.gist: Each assessment is marked Red, Amber or Green, which tells you how AI can be used in that assignment.

points.quote: The use of Gen AI tools (eg ChatGPT, DeepSeek, etc) is not permitted.
points.gist: In Red assessments, use of Gen AI tools such as ChatGPT or DeepSeek is not permitted.

points.quote: We encourage you to use Generative AI tools to help you with preparing this assessment.
points.gist: In Amber assessments, students are encouraged to use Generative AI tools to help prepare the assessment.

points.quote: Using Generative AI tools effectively is part of this assessment.
points.gist: In Green assessments, using Generative AI tools effectively is part of the assessment.

points.quote: It must not be used to write or create your coursework or assignments for you. This would be considered academic misconduct as described in UWL’s academic offences regulations.
points.anchor: How not to use AI and AI tools
points.gist: AI must not be used to write your coursework for you; doing so would be academic misconduct under UWL's academic offences regulations.

points.quote: You should always acknowledge the use of AI, just like any other source, and reference it correctly.
points.gist: You should always acknowledge AI use like any other source and reference it correctly.

points.quote: If an AI source has directed you to another webpage or a document and it is information on this page or in this document you are using in your course work or assignment, it is the webpage or the document you need to reference.
points.anchor: How to reference AI tools and AI generated content
points.gist: If an AI tool points you to a webpage or document you use, you need to reference that webpage or document.

points.quote: Not uploading someone else’s content to an AI tool where you don’t have permission to do this. This includes published sources as well as information you may have from live case studies used in your classes and client information you may be working with.
points.anchor: What does it mean when people say use AI ethically?
points.gist: Do not upload someone else's content without permission, including published sources, live case study information and client information.

points.quote: Not processing personal or confidential information. For example, uncoded responses from a research survey.
points.anchor: What does it mean when people say use AI ethically?
points.gist: Do not process personal or confidential information, for example uncoded responses from a research survey.

points.quote: The University of West London has opted to use Microsoft Copilot and Adobe Express as its base AI technologies.
points.gist: The University of West London uses Microsoft Copilot and Adobe Express as its base AI technologies.

points.quote: To keep your data as private as possible, UWL recommends you use Copilot. Inputting confidential information into AI tools could breach GDPR and professional society ethics codes.
points.anchor: What is meant by data privacy in an AI tool?
points.gist: UWL recommends Copilot to keep data as private as possible; inputting confidential information into AI tools could breach GDPR and professional ethics codes.

points.quote: You should never rely on AI as a substitute for reading research, official sources of law or regulatory codes. Information provided by AI must be cross-checked against these sources.
points.anchor: How not to use AI and AI tools
points.gist: Never rely on AI instead of reading research, law or regulatory codes; AI information must be cross-checked against these sources.

points.quote: An AI tool may also provide you with hallucinations of citations, providing a reference to a journal article, law case or other format which doesn’t exist. Always check the citation details to check they are real and reliable.
points.gist: AI tools may give references to articles or cases that do not exist, so always check citation details are real and reliable.

points.quote: Ownership (not uploading your work to non-UWL tools or giving it to other students).
points.gist: Academic integrity includes ownership: not uploading your work to non-UWL tools or giving it to other students.

points.quote: We encourage students are encouraged to use AI tools mindfully due to their environmental impact, in a similar way to the mindful use of paper and printing.
points.gist: Students are encouraged to use AI tools mindfully because of their environmental impact, like mindful use of paper and printing.

points.quote: AI can summarise a transcript of your lecture to help you discover the key points, when you have permission to do this.
points.gist: AI can summarise a lecture transcript to help find key points, when you have permission to do this.
